lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-9054 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/rchen
Date of birth: 5 Feb 1998 | Nationality: Singaporean
EDUCATION
Harbor State University | B.B.A. in Finance | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Stonebridge Manufacturing | Financial Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jan 2023 - Jun 2025
- Improved close efficiency by 40% by automating reconciliations and intercompany eliminations.
- Modeled the capital plan for 12 plant projects in a shared NPV template, so every request used the same discount rate and payback rules.
- Wrote the variance commentary for the monthly board pack, explaining each line more than 5% off budget.
- Valued the acquisition target by discounting its free cash flow to equity at the company's weighted average cost of capital.
- Reported a 45% group EBITDA margin by adding the EBITDA margins of the three business units.
- Built the rolling 18-month cash-flow forecast for a USD 600M manufacturer, keeping monthly forecast error under 4% and letting treasury pay down USD 40M of revolver debt early.
Crescent Bank | Credit Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2020 - Dec 2022
- Owned the credit reviews for the small-business loan book and the watch list the lending officers used.
- Reviewed 3 years of declined applications; the findings changed two ratio thresholds and raised approvals from 41% to 48% with no rise in early defaults.
- Wrote the covenant-monitoring checklist for the portfolio, cutting missed covenant tests from 7 to 1 a year.
- Built a spreading template for borrower financials that cut each credit memo from 6 hours to 3.
PROJECTS
Regional Utility Valuation | Independent Project | Excel | Nov 2024 - Present
- Valued a listed regional utility with a 10-year DCF and a comparable-company check, landing within 6% of the market price.
- Tested the valuation's sensitivity: a 1-point change in the discount rate moved the share value from USD 52 to USD 44.
- Shared the model and a two-page note with the university investment club, which used it in its spring pitch.
Student Investment Fund | Analyst, Team of 6 | Excel | Sep 2018 - May 2019
- Supported the FP&A team with financial reporting and analysis.
- Rebuilt the fund's performance report to show returns against its benchmark, which the committee used at every meeting.
- Built an 18-month cash forecast for a USD 600M business, holding error to about 4% and freeing USD 40M to repay debt early.
SKILLS
Tools: Excel, Bloomberg Terminal
Methods: financial modeling, DCF valuaton, forecasting, credit analysis

items.says: The date of birth and nationality are personal details that should not appear on the résumé.
items.because: They are not evidence of qualifications and use space without helping readers assess experience.

items.says: EDUCATION appears before professional experience.
items.because: Several years of experience make the career context more important to show first.

items.says: The 40% close-efficiency improvement has no defined measure or comparison period.
items.because: Readers cannot tell what became more efficient or how the change was measured.

items.says: The explanation of the template’s standardization purpose is wordy.
The variance-commentary line repeats the idea of explaining results and omits what the commentary enabled.
items.because: The 5% threshold describes the work’s scope, not its value to the board or business.

items.says: Free cash flow to equity is discounted at WACC rather than the cost of equity.
items.because: Using WACC with free cash flow to equity describes an inconsistent valuation method.

items.says: The valuation result and how it was used are unstated.
items.because: The method alone does not show the analysis’s scale or significance.

items.says: Adding business-unit EBITDA margins does not calculate a group EBITDA margin.
items.because: The group margin requires total EBITDA divided by total revenue, so the stated calculation does not support 45%.

items.says: The calculation clause delays the 45% figure, which lacks a reporting period and stated use.
items.because: Without a period or business use, the figure is hard to interpret and its value to leadership is unclear.

items.says: The forecast-error figure lacks a measure and evaluation period.
items.because: Forecast error can be calculated in different ways, and readers cannot tell how long it stayed under 4%.

items.says: The debt reduction is phrased as an indirect consequence and does not lead the line.
items.because: Opening with the forecast and accuracy delays the clearest business outcome.

items.says: The credit-review line describes responsibilities without assessment inputs, actions, or a result.
items.because: Readers cannot judge the assessments or tell what changed because of the reviews.

items.says: The early-default comparison has no stated period or baseline.
items.because: Readers cannot tell what “no rise” is compared against.

items.says: The strongest outcome does not lead the sentence.
items.because: Leading with the review process delays the threshold changes and approval increase on a quick scan.

items.says: The sensitivity line omits the direction and unit of the discount-rate change.
items.because: Readers cannot tell what the share-value movement represents or whether “1-point” means one percentage point.

items.says: “Which used it” does not identify whether the club used the model, the note, or both.
The FP&A line does not identify the specific work or its outcome.
items.because: Readers cannot tell what was prepared or analyzed, what changed, or how the activity connects to the fund.

items.says: The committee’s use of the report is delayed instead of leading the line.
items.because: Burying the clearest evidence of the report’s value makes it less visible on a quick scan.

items.says: The cash-forecast achievement appears under two roles, while its error measure and construction are unclear.
items.because: An almost identical forecast and outcome appears under Stonebridge years later, and the line does not define the error comparison or explain how the forecast was built.

items.says: The Student Investment Fund entry is difficult to place in the career story.
items.because: Its generic FP&A description and repeated cash-forecast claim make the older entry compete with more relevant experience.

items.says: “Valuaton” misspells “valuation.”
items.because: The misspelling in a skills term makes the line look unchecked.
